findings.title: `get_typed_config(..., int)` accepts bools, corrupting the new idle timeout
findings.description: `src/squadron/config/manager.py:109-140` adds a bool overload and correctly checks `type_ is bool` before `int`, but the `int` branch still uses `isinstance(value, int)`. Because `bool` is a subclass of `int`, a TOML value such as `"pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s" = true` returns `True` from an `int` typed read. `load_config()` in the same file merges TOML values with no schema validation, so this can bypass `set_config()` coercion. The new key in `src/squadron/config/keys.py:98-128` is consumed by `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py#_background_idle_timeout_s` and passed to `asyncio.timeout()` in `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:181-352`; `true`/`false` become a 1-second or immediate timeout instead of a clear configuration error. Reject `bool` for integer/float reads, validate the timeout as positive at the boundary, and add a regression test using a hand-written TOML bool.

findings.title: Async SDK dispatch performs blocking TOML reads while waiting on the stream
findings.description: `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:181-352` calls `_background_idle_timeout_s()` from the async receive loop. That helper calls `get_typed_config()`, which reaches `load_config()`/`_read_toml()` in `src/squadron/config/manager.py:48-93`; those functions synchronously open and parse both user and project TOML files. The Python rules require synchronous work inside `async def` to be under 1ms unless offloaded; disk I/O has no such bound and can block the event loop. The same pattern appears in `open_pipeline_session()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:445-470` and `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry()` in `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py:131-153`. Resolve these settings before entering the async loop or use `asyncio.to_thread`; also add an observable timeout/log or metric for a hung config read so this new I/O failure mode satisfies failure-mode enumeration.

findings.title: `ReviewTemplate.setting_sources` declares “never None” but the contract is not enforced
findings.description: The diff at `src/squadron/review/templates/__init__.py:31-40` changes the field to `list[str]` and documents that absent/null YAML resolves to `REVIEW_SETTING_SOURCES`, but only `load_template()` performs that resolution. Direct `ReviewTemplate(...)` construction is still a public boundary, and changed tests still pass `setting_sources=None`, e.g. `tests/review/test_review_client.py:35` and `tests/review/test_templates.py:186`. `run_review_with_profile()` at `src/squadron/review/review_client.py:212-220` trusts the value, and `ClaudeSDKProvider.create_agent()` at `src/squadron/providers/sdk/provider.py:77-91` omits `setting_sources` when the config value is `None` — the exact CLI-default behavior D9/D10 is trying to eliminate. Validate in `__post_init__`/Pydantic or resolve `None` in `run_review_with_profile()` before building `AgentConfig`, and add a test that a directly constructed SDK review template cannot reach the provider with `setting_sources=None`.

findings.title: New SDK background-wait path lacks a `tests/load/` regression test
findings.description: The new tests in `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py:810-1157` cover functional message scripts, idle timeout, stop-task failure, and unusable reconnect state, but `tests/load/` contains only `tests/load/test_grep_timeout.py` and `tests/load/test_worktree_concurrency.py`. There is no load test for this concurrency/environment-layer path exercising realistic multiple dispatches, many task lifecycle messages, or event-loop responsiveness under the new wait loop in `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:181-352`. The Python/testing rules require a load test on this tier that asserts latency, throughput, or resource bounds, and CI must gate it. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `uv run pytest`, so a new `tests/load/` test would be gated; add one that asserts event-loop responsiveness and bounded latency/resource behavior under background-task streams.

findings.title: Leftover injected turns discard text but not background-task ledger state
findings.description: D6 says that when an injected result arrives before the current dispatch’s own result, every message read so far belongs to the previous step. `SDKExecutionSession._collect_turns()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:205-230` implements that by calling `turns.discard()`, but `DispatchTurns.discard()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_turns.py:125-134` only clears `parts`. `BackgroundLedger.observe()` at `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_turns.py:49-65` may already have recorded `TaskStartedMessage`/terminal task state into `_active` and `_seen`, so the current dispatch can inherit previous-step waiting state and `background_tasks_waited` metadata. The existing leftover test in `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py:810-1157` uses only text plus an injected result, so it cannot catch this. Reset all per-turn state on discard (ledger, `own_result_seen`, `waiting_logged`, `progressed`) or explicitly scope the ledger to the current turn, and add a test where the discarded injected turn contains task lifecycle messages.

findings.title: Review prompt/settings comment contradicts the rendered sentinel
findings.description: The new comment in `src/squadron/review/models.py:213-217` says a `None` value renders as “not reported”, but `_render_optional()` in `src/squadron/review/persistence.py:317-326` returns `_NOT_COMPUTED` (`"not computed"`). The digest tests in `tests/review/test_persistence.py:1600-1650` and the checked-in `tests/review/fixtures/clean_pass_artifact.md` also assert `"not computed"`. Update the field comment to match the shared sentinel or change the renderer and tests consistently; leaving the drift makes the public model documentation misleading.
